description: Use this when the user wants to publish, draft or schedule a BLOG POST on their WordPress site. Publishing costs no credits. A title is REQUIRED and the text becomes the body: plain text or light markdown (## headings, - lists, **bold**, [links](url)) is turned into WordPress blocks, and HTML is sent as written. status: publish (default), draft, pending (submit for review), private (logged-in editors only) or future with a date — a future `date` makes WordPress schedule it natively. The FIRST image becomes the FEATURED image, every other image is uploaded and placed inline, and a video is uploaded and embedded (if the site's host refuses the file as too large, the post plays it from its own link and the reply says so). categories and tags take names or ids; a name the site lacks is CREATED and the reply says which. An over-long title is refused, never cut. WordPress has NO per-post views in its API: never quote a view count for a WordPress post. Self-hosted WordPress only — a WordPress.com site needs its own OAuth sign-in and cannot be connected. Not connected: the user connects it under Connectors > WordPress, or you call connect_connector with provider wordpress (siteUrl, username, appPassword).

allowDuplicate.description: post it even though an identical post was just made

brand.description: WHICH PROFILE this post belongs to — id or exact name from list_brands (a shared workspace: its profile id). Beats the connection's pin for THIS CALL ONLY; a name that matches no profile, or two, is REFUSED and nothing is posted.

categories.description: category names or ids (a missing name is created)

date.description: ISO time to publish at; a future date schedules it on WordPress itself

excerpt.description: the summary under the title in lists and search

ideaId.description: short id of the content-plan idea this post came from

idempotencyKey.description: any stable string: a repeat within 24h returns the original post instead of posting again

imageUrl.description: one image — becomes the featured image

imageUrls.description: several images: the first is featured, the rest go inline

recipe.description: the post's FORMAT id, e.g. "slideshow" or "imessage_chat" — post_performance groups by it, so reuse one id per format

slug.description: the end of the post URL

tags.description: tag names or ids (a missing name is created)

text.description: the body: plain text, light markdown or HTML

videoUrl.description: one video, embedded in the post

name: post_to_wordpress
title: Publish a WordPress blog post
